practices.practice: Read the DocumentDB MongoDB-compatible connection string from an environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime and do not check it into source control or logs.
practices.prior_belief: Read the DocumentDB MongoDB-compatible connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) or a secret store at runtime; never check the connection string into source control or write it to logs.

practices.practice: Create one MongoClient/driver client and reuse it (process-wide singleton) rather than creating a new client per request; cache it across warm serverless invocations.
practices.prior_belief: Reuse a single Motor/PyMongo client across the app (create once at startup and inject), set a sensible maxPoolSize/minPoolSize rather than creating a new client per request to avoid connection storms.

practices.practice: Always connect with TLS enabled and do not disable certificate validation in production (ensure CA bundles or proper TLS configuration instead).
practices.prior_belief: Enable TLS/SSL on the client connection and verify certificates (tls=true or tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=false) so traffic to the managed cluster is encrypted in transit.

practices.practice: Use least-privilege credentials for applications (create per-app users or use Microsoft Entra ID / managed identity + RBAC) instead of using admin/root accounts.
practices.prior_belief: Use least-privilege database credentials: create a dedicated DB user for the sample app with only the minimal roles (readWrite on sample_fintech_10) rather than using an admin/root account.

practices.practice: Include a schema or classifier version (and model identifier/dimensions where vectors are used) alongside vectors and indexable metadata so you can interpret and rebuild results later.
Embed small, bounded arrays (one-to-few) inside the parent document when children are always read together; avoid embedding unbounded arrays that could approach BSON size limits.
practices.prior_belief: For expense reports with many small line items, embed the line_item array inside the parent report document (rather than separate collection) when typical array sizes are small (dozens) and you always fetch the whole report; avoid embedding huge arrays to stay well under the DB document size limit.

practices.practice: Model frequently-updated or unbounded children (e.g., line items that are queried/updated individually or can grow large) as a separate collection with a reference and index on the parent id.
practices.prior_belief: If you need to query or update individual line items frequently or arrays can grow large, model line items as a separate collection with report_id reference and index on report_id to keep single-document sizes small and make updates idempotent.

practices.practice: Design compound indexes that match the app’s common query shapes following the ESR rule (Equality → Sort → Range) so queries and sorts can be served by an index without blocking in-memory sorts.
practices.prior_belief: Create compound indexes that match the app’s common queries exactly (e.g., {company_id:1, report_status:1, submitted_at:-1}) so the query planner can use index prefixes; verify with explain() that indexes are used.

practices.practice: Ensure fields used in sort operations are included in an index (or index prefix) to avoid blocking in-memory sorts and high memory use.
practices.prior_belief: Add an index on any field used in sort operations (e.g., submitted_at) to avoid in-memory sorts and high memory utilization during queries.

practices.practice: Use partial or sparse indexes for optional or rarely-populated fields (e.g., policy_violation:true) to reduce index size and write cost when appropriate.
practices.prior_belief: Use partial or sparse indexes for optional or rare fields you query (e.g., policy_violation:true) to keep index size down and speed writes.

practices.practice: Plan index changes safely: inventory existing indexes, detect redundancy, hide an index to test, build/drop during low-traffic windows and monitor impact rather than doing blind index changes in production.

For vector search, create a matching vector index (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF) with the correct dimensionality and similarity and tune build/search params (e.g., lBuild, lSearch, maxDegree) for your recall/latency tradeoff.
practices.prior_belief: For vector search, persist vectors as a numeric array field and create the appropriate vector index (HNSW/IVF/DiskANN) with matching parameters (distance metric: cosine or inner_product, M/ef_construction or ef_search) tuned to vector dimensionality and recall/latency needs.

practices.practice: Normalize/store the embedding dimensionality and persist model identifiers with vectors, and index metadata fields (company_id, report_id) so ANN queries can pre-filter by metadata before nearest-neighbour search.
practices.prior_belief: Normalize the vector dimensionality (consistent embedding length) and store metadata fields indexed for filtering (e.g., company_id, report_id) so vector queries can be filtered by metadata before nearest-neighbour search.

practices.practice: Implement idempotent processing using an atomic state change (e.g., findOneAndUpdate with a processing_status filter) or use optimistic concurrency (ETag/_etag) to prevent double-processing in retries.
practices.prior_belief: Implement idempotency and optimistic concurrency for processing reports: use a processing_status field with atomic updates (findOneAndUpdate with a status filter) or include an etag/_id-based check to avoid double-processing when retries occur.

practices.practice: Use retries with exponential backoff for transient network or rate-limit errors, catch driver-specific retryable exceptions, and bound total retry time to avoid long blocking operations.
practices.prior_belief: Use retry with exponential backoff for transient network and rate-limit errors; capture specific retryable exception classes from Motor/PyMongo and limit total retry time to avoid long blocking operations.

practices.practice: Avoid long-running, large multi-document transactions for classifier pipelines; prefer single-document atomic updates or small transactions scoped to the partition key.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid long-running transactions across many documents for the classifier pipeline; prefer single-document atomic updates or small multi-document transactions limited to what the MongoDB/Cosmos API supports.
practices.how_found: Azure Cosmos DB transactions optimistic concurrency

practices.practice: Log slow or high-latency queries, capture timestamps and correlation ids, and use explain("executionStats") and provider tooling (MCP/diagnostic logs) to inspect query plans and index usage.
practices.prior_belief: Log queries that exceed a latency threshold and use explain() and the provider's tools (the provided MCP server tools) to inspect query plans and index usage; include timestamps and correlation ids in logs for each processed report.

practices.practice: Never persist API keys or plaintext credentials (LLM keys or DB admin passwords) in the database; keep secrets in a secret store (Key Vault) or use managed identities.
practices.prior_belief: Do not persist LLM API keys or plaintext credentials in the DB; if storing model-related config, store only non-sensitive version identifiers and minimal configuration and keep secrets in environment or Key Vault.

practices.practice: Make seed and demo scripts idempotent (create-if-not-exists / upsert semantics) and target the intended database name so repeated runs are safe.
practices.prior_belief: Seed test/demo data and create indexes programmatically (seed script + indexes module) against the specific database name (sample_fintech_10) but ensure scripts are idempotent (create_if_not_exists semantics) so repeated runs are safe.

practices.practice: Persist agent/session memory or ephemeral classification decisions with explicit versioning and, if ephemeral, a TTL; include deterministic-fallback flags to allow replayable deterministic tests.
practices.prior_belief: Persist agent memory or consistent classification decisions in the DB with versioning and TTL for ephemeral session memory; include a deterministic fallback flag so replayable tests can run without an LLM key.

practices.practice: Use the $search aggregation stage with the cosmosSearch operator for kNN vector queries, tune k and lSearch (keep lSearch ≥ k), and push equality/range/geospatial pre-filters into the operator's filter field rather than post-filtering.
Prefer provider-supported full-text/search (DocumentDB's textSearch/$search) features over community $text where available for better integration and scoring.

Be aware of driver and API feature differences across supported MongoDB wire versions; check the provider's feature-support matrix for operations like retryable writes, findAndModify, sessions and transaction support before relying on them.

practices.practice: Tune connection pool parameters to your deployment type: small pools for serverless warm-invocations (maxPoolSize 3–5), larger pools for long-running OLTP servers, and short maxIdleTime for serverless to avoid idle connections.
